source_text: Καὶ πάλιν ὡς αὐτολεξεὶ διὰ παρθένου μὲν τεχθησόμενος διὰ τοῦ Ἡσαΐου προεφητεύθη, ἀκούσατε. Ἐλέχθη δὲ οὕτως· „Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ ἐροῦσιν ἐπὶ τᾷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ Μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός“. Ἃ γὰρ ἦν ἄπιστα καὶ ἀδύνατα νομιζόμενα παρὰ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις γενήσεσθαι, ταῦτα ὁ θεὸς προεμήνυσε διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος μέλλειν γίνεσθαι, ἵνα ὅταν γένηται μὴ ἀπιστηθῇ, ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ τοῦ προειρῆσθαι πιστευθῇ. Ὅπως δὲ μή τινες, μὴ νοήσαντες τὴν δεδηλωμένην προφητείαν, ἐγκαλέσωσιν ἡμῖν ἅπερ ἐνεκαλέσαμεν τοῖς ποιηταῖς, εἰποῦσιν ἀφροδισίων χάριν ἐληλυθέναι ἐπὶ γυναῖκας τὸν Δία, διασαφῆσαι τοὺς λόγους πειρασόμεθα. Τὸ οὖν „Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει“ σημαίνει οὐ συνουσιασθεῖσαν τὴν παρθένον συλλαβεῖν· εἰ γὰρ ἐσυνουσιάσθη ὑπὸ ὁτουοῦν, οὐκ ἔτι ἦν παρθένος· ἀλλὰ δύναμις θεοῦ ἐπελθοῦσα τῇ παρθένῳ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτήν, καὶ κυοφορῆσαι παρθένον οὖσαν πεποίηκε. Καὶ ὁ ἀποσταλεὶς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν τὴν παρθένον κατ᾿ ἐκεῖνο τοῦ καιροῦ ἄγγελος θεοῦ εὐηγγελίσατο αὐτὴν εἰπών· „Ἰδοὺ συλλήψῃ ἐν γαστρὶ ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου καὶ τέξῃ υἱόν, καὶ υἱὸς ὑψίστου κληθήσεται, καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν“, ὡς οἱ ἀπομνημονεύσαντες πάντα τὰ περὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐδίδαξαν, οἷς ἐπιστεύσαμεν, ἐπειδὴ καὶ διὰ Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προδεδηλωμένου τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα τοῦτον γεννησόμενον, ὡς προεμηνύομεν, ἔφη. Τὸ πνεῦμα οὖν καὶ. τὴν δύναμιν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐδὲν ἄλλο νοῆσαι θέμις ἢ τὸν λόγον, ὃς καὶ πρωτότοκος τῷ θεῷ ἐστι, Μωϋσῆς ὁ προδεδηλωμένος προφήτης ἐμήνυσε· καὶ τοῦτο ἐλθὸν ἐπὶ τὴν παρθένον καὶ ἐπισκιάσαν οὐ διὰ συνουσίας ἀλλὰ διὰ δυνάμεως ἐγκύμονα κατέστησε. Τὸ δὲ Ἰησοῦς, ὄνομα τῇ ἑβραΐδι φωνῇ, σωτὴρ τῇ ἑλληνίδι διαλέκτῳ δηλοῖ. Ὅθεν καὶ ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸς τὴν παρθένον εἶπε· „Καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν· αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν“. Ὅτι δὲ οὐδενὶ ἄλλῳ θεοφοροῦνται οἱ προφητεύοντες εἰ μὴ λόγῳ θείῳ, καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὡς ὑπολαμβάνω, φήσετε.
pass_a_gloss: And again, as it has been spoken by himself, through a virgin he is going to be born, it was foretold through Isaiah, listen. It was spoken thus: 'Behold, the virgin will have in womb and will bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel, which is God with us.' For what was considered unbelievable and impossible to happen among men, God foretold through the prophetic Spirit that it was going to happen, so that when it happens it may not be disbelieved, but believed because it was foretold. And so that some people, not understanding the prophecy that has been spoken, may not accuse us of what we accused the poets, saying that Zeus came to women for the sake of lust, we will try to explain the words. The 'Behold, the virgin will have in womb' means that the virgin, not having intercourse, conceived; for if she had intercourse with someone, she would no longer be a virgin; but the power of God, having come upon the virgin, overshadowed her, and made the virgin, while still a virgin, pregnant. And the angel sent to the virgin at that time announced the good news to her, saying: 'Behold, you will conceive in womb from the Holy Spirit and will bear a son, and he will be called the son of the Most High, and you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins,' as those who remembered all things about our Savior Jesus Christ taught, whom we believed, since also through Isaiah the prophetic Spirit foretold that this one was going to be born, as we foretold. The Spirit, therefore, and the power from God, it is not right to understand as anything else but the Word, who is also the firstborn of God, Moses the foretold prophet foretold; and this, having come upon the virgin and overshadowed her, not through intercourse but through power, made her pregnant. And the name Jesus, in the Hebrew language, means Savior in the Greek dialect. From which also the angel said to the virgin: 'And you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.' That the prophets prophesy borne by no other than the divine Word, you also, as I suppose, will say.

pass_b_english: Once again, just as it was spoken by himself, it was foretold through Isaiah that he would be born through a virgin; listen. It was spoken in this way: "Behold, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel," which means "God with us" (Isaiah 7:14). For the things that were considered unbelievable and impossible among human beings, God foretold through the prophetic Spirit that they were going to happen, so that when they do happen they will not be disbelieved, but will be believed precisely because they were foretold. We will also try to explain the words so that certain people, failing to understand the prophecy that has been spoken, may not accuse us of the very thing we accused the poets of, namely, saying that Zeus came to women for the sake of lust. The statement "Behold, the virgin will conceive" means that the virgin conceived without having intercourse; for if she had intercourse with anyone, she would no longer be a virgin. Rather, the power of God came upon the virgin and overshadowed her, and made her pregnant while she remained a virgin. And the angel of God sent to the virgin at that time announced the good news to her, saying: "Behold, you will conceive in your womb from the Holy Spirit and will bear a son, and he will be called the Son of the Most High, and you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins" (Matthew 1:21), just as those who remembered all things about our Savior Jesus Christ taught, and we believed them, since through Isaiah, the prophetic Spirit foretold that this one was going to be born, as we declared beforehand. The Spirit, therefore, and the power from God, it is not right to understand as anything other than the Word, who is also the firstborn of God, as Moses, the foretold prophet, foretold; and this Word, having come upon the virgin and overshadowed her, made her pregnant not through intercourse but through power. And the name Jesus, in the Hebrew language, means Savior in the Greek dialect. From this the angel also said to the virgin: "And you will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins." That the prophets prophesy carried by no other than the divine Word, you also, as I suppose, will say.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful literal translation, and Pass B provides a fluent version with correct scripture citations (Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:21) corresponding to the quoted text. All nuances regarding the distinction between intercourse (συνουσίας) and power (δυνάμεως) are preserved.
